requirements.original: Messages are instances of types declared in the in/out/inout clauses of message port type definition.
requirements.canonical: A message IS an instance of a type declared in the `in`, `out` or `inout` clause of a message port type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 13 -- Messages are instances of types declared in the in/out/inout clauses of message port type definition.

requirements.original: Any type can be declared as type of a message in a message port type definition, i.e. values of any basic or structured type (see clauses 6.1 and 6.2) can be sent or received.
requirements.canonical: Any type MAY be declared as the type of a message in a message port type definition.

ambiguity.issue: "Any type" is narrowed by the "i.e." clause to basic and structured types; it is unclear whether non-data types (e.g. port, component, default or timer types) may also be message types. The canonical text keeps the literal wording.
readings: Any type, including non-data types, MAY be declared as the type of a message in a message port type definition.
Any data type (a basic type or a structured type) MAY be declared as the type of a message in a message port type definition.

examples.text:
// a structured, ordered message with two fields
  type record ARecord { integer i, float f }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 13 -- Any type can be declared as type of a message in a message port type definition, i.e. values of any basic or structured type (see clauses 6.1 and 6.2) can be sent or received.

requirements.original: Any type can be declared as type of a message in a message port type definition, i.e. values of any basic or structured type (see clauses 6.1 and 6.2) can be sent or received.
requirements.canonical: A value of any basic type or structured type MAY be sent or received as a message.

examples.text:
// a structured, ordered message with two fields
  type record ARecord { integer i, float f }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 13 -- Any type can be declared as type of a message in a message port type definition, i.e. values of any basic or structured type (see clauses 6.1 and 6.2) can be sent or received.

requirements.original: Received messages can also be declared as a combination of value and matching mechanisms (see clause 15.5).
requirements.canonical: A template used to receive a message MAY be declared as a combination of values and matching mechanisms.

ambiguity.issue: A received message is a value; what is declared as a combination of values and matching mechanisms is the template used in the receiving operation.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 13 -- Received messages can also be declared as a combination of value and matching mechanisms (see clause 15.5).

requirements.original: Instances of messages can be declared by global, local or in-line templates (see clause 15.0) or being constructed and passed via variables or template variables (see clause 11) and parameters or template parameters (see clause 5.4).
requirements.canonical: A message MAY be declared by a global, local or in-line template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 13 -- Instances of messages can be declared by global, local or in-line templates (see clause 15.0) or being constructed and passed via variables or template variables (see clause 11) and parameters or template parameters (see clause 5.4).

requirements.original: Instances of messages can be declared by global, local or in-line templates (see clause 15.0) or being constructed and passed via variables or template variables (see clause 11) and parameters or template parameters (see clause 5.4).
requirements.canonical: A message MAY be constructed and passed via a variable or a template variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 13 -- Instances of messages can be declared by global, local or in-line templates (see clause 15.0) or being constructed and passed via variables or template variables (see clause 11) and parameters or template parameters (see clause 5.4).

requirements.original: Instances of messages can be declared by global, local or in-line templates (see clause 15.0) or being constructed and passed via variables or template variables (see clause 11) and parameters or template parameters (see clause 5.4).
requirements.canonical: A message MAY be passed via a value formal parameter or a template formal parameter.

ambiguity.issue: "parameters or template parameters" refers to value and template formal parameters (see clause 5.4).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 13 -- Instances of messages can be declared by global, local or in-line templates (see clause 15.0) or being constructed and passed via variables or template variables (see clause 11) and parameters or template parameters (see clause 5.4).

requirements.original: Procedure signatures (or signatures for short) are needed for procedure-based communication.
requirements.canonical: Procedure-based communication SHALL be based on procedure signatures.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- Procedure signatures (or signatures for short) are needed for procedure-based communication.

requirements.original: Procedure-based communication may be used for the communication within the test system, i.e. among test components, or for the communication between the test system and the SUT.
requirements.canonical: Procedure-based communication MAY be used for the communication among test components within the test system.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- Procedure-based communication may be used for the communication within the test system, i.e. among test components, or for the communication between the test system and the SUT.

requirements.original: Procedure-based communication may be used for the communication within the test system, i.e. among test components, or for the communication between the test system and the SUT.
requirements.canonical: Procedure-based communication MAY be used for the communication between the test system and the SUT.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- Procedure-based communication may be used for the communication within the test system, i.e. among test components, or for the communication between the test system and the SUT.

requirements.original: In the latter case, a procedure may either be invoked in the SUT (i.e. the test system performs the call) or in the test system (i.e. the SUT performs the call).
requirements.canonical: If procedure-based communication is used between the test system and the SUT, a remote procedure MAY be invoked either in the SUT (the test system performs the call) or in the test system (the SUT performs the call).
requirements.condition: procedure-based communication is used between the test system and the SUT
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- In the latter case, a procedure may either be invoked in the SUT (i.e. the test system performs the call) or in the test system (i.e. the SUT performs the call).

requirements.original: signature SignatureIdentifier "(" { [ in | inout | out ] Type ValueParIdentifier [ ","] } ")" [ ( return TypeOrNestedTypeDef ) | noblock ] [ exception "(" ExceptionTypeList ")" ]
requirements.canonical: A signature definition has the syntax `signature` SignatureIdentifier "(" { [ `in` | `inout` | `out` ] Type ValueParIdentifier [","] } ")" [ ( `return` TypeOrNestedTypeDef ) | `noblock` ] [ `exception` "(" ExceptionTypeList ")" ].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- signature SignatureIdentifier "(" { [ in | inout | out ] Type ValueParIdentifier [ ","] } ")" [ ( return TypeOrNestedTypeDef ) | noblock ] [ exception "(" ExceptionTypeList ")" ]

requirements.original: For all used procedures, i.e. procedures used for the communication among test components, procedures called from the SUT and procedures called from the test system, a procedure signature shall be defined in the TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: A procedure signature SHALL be defined in the TTCN-3 module for every procedure used for procedure-based communication among test components, called from the SUT or called from the test system.

ambiguity.issue: "the TTCN-3 module" does not say which module; signatures may be imported (clause 8.2.3), so the most likely reading is that the signature is defined in some TTCN-3 module visible to the user, not necessarily the using module.
readings: A procedure signature SHALL be defined in some TTCN-3 module (possibly imported) for every used procedure.
A procedure signature SHALL be defined in the same TTCN-3 module in which the procedure is used.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- For all used procedures, i.e. procedures used for the communication among test components, procedures called from the SUT and procedures called from the test system, a procedure signature shall be defined in the TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports blocking and non-blocking procedure-based communication.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language supports blocking and non-blocking procedure-based communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- TTCN-3 supports blocking and non-blocking procedure-based communication.

requirements.original: By default, signature definitions without the noblock keyword are assumed to be used for blocking procedure-based communication.
requirements.canonical: A signature definition without the `noblock` keyword IS used for blocking procedure-based communication.
requirements.condition: the signature definition does not contain the noblock keyword
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- By default, signature definitions without the noblock keyword are assumed to be used for blocking procedure-based communication.

requirements.original: Signature definitions may have parameters.
requirements.canonical: A signature definition MAY have signature parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- Signature definitions may have parameters.

requirements.original: Parameters shall be of data type only, i.e. of a basic type, a structured type thereof or a subtype thereof.
requirements.canonical: A signature parameter SHALL be of a data type only, i.e. of a basic type, a structured type thereof or a subtype thereof.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- Parameters shall be of data type only, i.e. of a basic type, a structured type thereof or a subtype thereof.

requirements.original: Within a signature definition the parameter list may include parameter identifiers, parameter types and their direction, i.e. in, out, or inout.
requirements.canonical: The parameter list of a signature definition MAY include parameter identifiers, parameter types and their direction (`in`, `out` or `inout`).

ambiguity.issue: "may include" suggests all three items are optional, but the syntax (14-s004) makes the type and identifier mandatory for each parameter and only the direction optional. The canonical text keeps the literal reading; the syntax reading is the likely intent.
readings: Each signature parameter SHALL have a type and an identifier, and MAY have a direction (`in`, `out` or `inout`).
A signature parameter MAY omit its identifier, type or direction.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- Within a signature definition the parameter list may include parameter identifiers, parameter types and their direction, i.e. in, out, or inout.

requirements.original: The direction inout and out indicate that these parameters are used to retrieve information from the remote procedure.
requirements.canonical: A signature parameter with direction `inout` or `out` IS used to retrieve information from the remote procedure.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- The direction inout and out indicate that these parameters are used to retrieve information from the remote procedure.

requirements.original: NOTE 1: The direction of the parameters is as seen by the called party rather than the calling party.
requirements.canonical: The direction of a signature parameter IS as seen by the called party rather than by the calling party.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- NOTE 1: The direction of the parameters is as seen by the called party rather than the calling party.

requirements.original: A remote procedure may return a value after its termination.
requirements.canonical: A remote procedure MAY return a value after its termination.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- A remote procedure may return a value after its termination.

requirements.original: The type of the return value shall be of data type only and shall be specified by means of a return clause in the corresponding signature definition.
requirements.canonical: The return type of a signature SHALL be a data type only.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- The type of the return value shall be of data type only and shall be specified by means of a return clause in the corresponding signature definition.

requirements.original: The type of the return value shall be specified by means of a return clause in the corresponding signature definition.
requirements.canonical: If a remote procedure returns a value, the type of the return value SHALL be specified by a `return` clause in the corresponding signature definition.
requirements.condition: the remote procedure returns a value
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- The type of the return value shall be specified by means of a return clause in the corresponding signature definition.

requirements.original: Exceptions that may be raised by remote procedures are represented in TTCN-3 as values of a specific type.
requirements.canonical: An exception that may be raised by a remote procedure IS represented as a value of a specific type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- Exceptions that may be raised by remote procedures are represented in TTCN-3 as values of a specific type.

requirements.original: Therefore templates and matching mechanisms can be used to specify or check return values of remote procedures.
requirements.canonical: A template or a matching mechanism MAY be used to specify or check an exception raised by a remote procedure.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence starts with "Therefore" after a sentence about exceptions but speaks of "return values"; most likely "exceptions" (values of exception types) is meant. Both readings are true in the language.
readings: A template or a matching mechanism MAY be used to specify or check an exception raised by a remote procedure.
A template or a matching mechanism MAY be used to specify or check the return value of a remote procedure.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- Therefore templates and matching mechanisms can be used to specify or check return values of remote procedures.

requirements.original: The exceptions are defined in the form of an exception list included in the signature definition.
requirements.canonical: The exceptions of a signature ARE defined in the form of an exception list included in the signature definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- The exceptions are defined in the form of an exception list included in the signature definition.

requirements.original: This list defines all the possible different types associated with the set of possible exceptions (the meaning of exceptions themselves will usually only be distinguished by specific values of these types).
requirements.canonical: The exception list of a signature definition IS the set of all possible types of the exceptions that the remote procedure may raise.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- This list defines all the possible different types associated with the set of possible exceptions (the meaning of exceptions themselves will usually only be distinguished by specific values of these types).

requirements.original: a) Signature definitions for non-blocking communication shall use the noblock keyword, shall only have in parameters and shall have no return value but may raise exceptions.
requirements.canonical: A signature definition for non-blocking communication SHALL use the `noblock` keyword.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- a) Signature definitions for non-blocking communication shall use the noblock keyword, shall only have in parameters and shall have no return value but may raise exceptions.

requirements.original: a) Signature definitions for non-blocking communication shall use the noblock keyword, shall only have in parameters and shall have no return value but may raise exceptions.
requirements.canonical: A signature definition with the `noblock` keyword SHALL only have `in` parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- a) Signature definitions for non-blocking communication shall use the noblock keyword, shall only have in parameters and shall have no return value but may raise exceptions.

requirements.original: a) Signature definitions for non-blocking communication shall use the noblock keyword, shall only have in parameters and shall have no return value but may raise exceptions.
requirements.canonical: A signature definition with the `noblock` keyword SHALL NOT have a return value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- a) Signature definitions for non-blocking communication shall use the noblock keyword, shall only have in parameters and shall have no return value but may raise exceptions.

requirements.original: a) Signature definitions for non-blocking communication shall use the noblock keyword, shall only have in parameters and shall have no return value but may raise exceptions.
requirements.canonical: A signature definition with the `noblock` keyword MAY have an exception list.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- a) Signature definitions for non-blocking communication shall use the noblock keyword, shall only have in parameters and shall have no return value but may raise exceptions.

requirements.original: b) Signature parameters and the return type shall be of a data type.
requirements.canonical: A signature parameter SHALL be of a data type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- b) Signature parameters and the return type shall be of a data type.

requirements.original: b) Signature parameters and the return type shall be of a data type.
requirements.canonical: The return type of a signature SHALL be a data type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 14 -- b) Signature parameters and the return type shall be of a data type.

requirements.original: Templates can be defined globally or locally.
requirements.canonical: A template MAY be defined globally or locally.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- Templates can be defined globally or locally.

requirements.original: b) they can be parameterized;
requirements.canonical: A template MAY be parameterized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- b) they can be parameterized;

requirements.original: c) they allow matching mechanisms;
requirements.canonical: A template MAY contain matching mechanisms.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- c) they allow matching mechanisms;

requirements.original: d) they can be used with either message-based or procedure-based communications.
requirements.canonical: A template MAY be used with message-based communication or with procedure-based communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- d) they can be used with either message-based or procedure-based communications.

requirements.original: Within a template values, ranges and matching attributes can be specified and then used in both message-based and procedure-based communications.
requirements.canonical: A template MAY specify values, ranges and matching attributes, which MAY then be used in both message-based and procedure-based communication.

ambiguity.issue: 'matching attributes' is used instead of the standard term 'matching mechanisms'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- Within a template values, ranges and matching attributes can be specified and then used in both message-based and procedure-based communications.

requirements.original: Templates may be specified for any TTCN-3 type or procedure signature.
requirements.canonical: A template MAY be specified for any TTCN-3 type or procedure signature.

ambiguity.issue: Restriction a) of the same clause limits templates to component data types and signatures, so 'any TTCN-3 type' conflicts with it. Reading 2 is chosen, because the restriction is more specific.
readings: A template MAY be specified for every TTCN-3 type without exception, and for any procedure signature.
A template MAY be specified for any TTCN-3 type that is a component data type, and for any procedure signature.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- Templates may be specified for any TTCN-3 type or procedure signature.

requirements.original: The type-based templates are used for message-based communications and the signature templates are used in procedure-based communications.
requirements.canonical: A type-based (message) template IS used for message-based communication.

ambiguity.issue: 'type-based templates' is used for what clause 15.1 and 15.3 call 'message templates'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- The type-based templates are used for message-based communications and the signature templates are used in procedure-based communications.

requirements.original: The type-based templates are used for message-based communications and the signature templates are used in procedure-based communications.
requirements.canonical: A signature template IS used for procedure-based communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- The type-based templates are used for message-based communications and the signature templates are used in procedure-based communications.

requirements.original: A template can be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.
requirements.canonical: A template declaration MAY contain the `@fuzzy` modifier to declare the template as fuzzy.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- A template can be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.

requirements.original: NOTE: Using a fuzzy template from a non-fuzzy template causes evaluation of the fuzzy template.
requirements.canonical: When a fuzzy template is used from a non-fuzzy template, the fuzzy template IS evaluated.
requirements.condition: a fuzzy template is referenced from a non-fuzzy template
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- NOTE: Using a fuzzy template from a non-fuzzy template causes evaluation of the fuzzy template.

requirements.original: Thus, for unparameterized non-fuzzy templates, the result of the used fuzzy templates will stay the same for every usage. NOTE: Using a fuzzy template from a non-fuzzy template causes evaluation of the fuzzy template.
requirements.canonical: For an unparameterized non-fuzzy template, the result of a fuzzy template used in it IS the same for every usage of the non-fuzzy template.
requirements.condition: the using template is unparameterized and non-fuzzy
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- Thus, for unparameterized non-fuzzy templates, the result of the used fuzzy templates will stay the same for every usage. NOTE: Using a fuzzy template from a non-fuzzy template causes evaluation of the fuzzy template.

requirements.original: A fuzzy template can be declared deterministic using the @deterministic modifier.
requirements.canonical: A fuzzy template declaration MAY contain the `@deterministic` modifier to declare the template as deterministic.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- A fuzzy template can be declared deterministic using the @deterministic modifier.

requirements.original: A deterministic template shall be evaluated to the same result in the same deterministic evaluation context whenever it is evaluated.
requirements.canonical: A deterministic template SHALL evaluate to the same result whenever it is evaluated in the same deterministic evaluation context.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- A deterministic template shall be evaluated to the same result in the same deterministic evaluation context whenever it is evaluated.

requirements.original: A modified template declaration (see clause 15.5) specifies only the fields to be changed from the base template, i.e. it is a partial specification.
requirements.canonical: A modified template declaration IS a partial specification that specifies only the fields to be changed from the base template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- A modified template declaration (see clause 15.5) specifies only the fields to be changed from the base template, i.e. it is a partial specification.

requirements.original: a) Templates shall be specified only for component data types and procedure signatures.
requirements.canonical: A template SHALL be specified only for a component data type or a procedure signature.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- a) Templates shall be specified only for component data types and procedure signatures.

requirements.original: c) The expression or template body initializing a template shall evaluate to a value or template, which is type compatible with the template being declared.
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body initializing a template SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is type compatible with the template being declared.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- c) The expression or template body initializing a template shall evaluate to a value or template, which is type compatible with the template being declared.

requirements.original: d) The expression or template body initializing a template shall evaluate to a value or a template that is at least partially initialized or to a matching mechanism.
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body initializing a template SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is at least partially initialized, or to a matching mechanism.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- d) The expression or template body initializing a template shall evaluate to a value or a template that is at least partially initialized or to a matching mechanism.

requirements.original: e) The body of a fuzzy template shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.
requirements.canonical: The body of a fuzzy template SHALL NOT contain calls of functions that have `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- e) The body of a fuzzy template shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.

requirements.original: The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.
requirements.canonical: A function called from the body of a fuzzy template MAY internally call other functions that have `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.condition: the function is called in the body of a fuzzy template
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.

requirements.original: f) Fuzzy features are valid only in the scope, where the templates' names are visible.
requirements.canonical: The fuzzy feature of a fuzzy template IS valid only in the scope where the name of the template is visible.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether 'the templates' names' means the name of the template declaration only, or also the names of formal parameters to which the template is passed (the following sentence implies that a fuzzy formal parameter keeps the feature). Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: The fuzzy feature IS valid only where the fuzzy template is referenced by its own name or through a formal template parameter declared `@fuzzy`.
The fuzzy feature IS valid only in the scope of the template declaration, and never inside a called function.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- f) Fuzzy features are valid only in the scope, where the templates' names are visible.

requirements.original: For example, if a fuzzy template is passed to a formal template parameter declared without a modifier, it loses its fuzzy feature inside the called function. f) Fuzzy features are valid only in the scope, where the templates' names are visible.
requirements.canonical: When a fuzzy template is passed to a formal template parameter declared without a modifier, the fuzzy template IS treated as non-fuzzy inside the called function.
requirements.condition: the fuzzy template is passed to a formal template parameter declared without a modifier
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- For example, if a fuzzy template is passed to a formal template parameter declared without a modifier, it loses its fuzzy feature inside the called function. f) Fuzzy features are valid only in the scope, where the templates' names are visible.

requirements.original: g) For a fuzzy template that is declared deterministic the template body shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.canonical: The template body of a fuzzy template that is declared `@deterministic` SHALL fulfil the restrictions on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- g) For a fuzzy template that is declared deterministic the template body shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.original: template @fuzzy charstring m_fuzzy := fx_garble("foobar"); // every usage of m_fuzzy re evaluates the function call
requirements.canonical: Every usage of a fuzzy template whose body is a function call IS a re-evaluation of the function call.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.0 -- template @fuzzy charstring m_fuzzy := fx_garble("foobar"); // every usage of m_fuzzy re evaluates the function call
